narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. The short nine-month duration of your requested credit actually worked in your favor, as it is well below the average of nineteen months seen among approved applicants and pushed the prediction toward good credit. However, this positive effect was outweighed by the other two factors. Requesting the loan for business purposes pulled the prediction toward bad credit, as business loans are relatively uncommon among approved applicants. More importantly, your checking account status of 0-200 DM was the strongest single factor driving the denial, as this balance level is associated with higher risk compared with the many approved applicants who have no checking account or larger balances.

Because your application was declined primarily due to your checking account balance and the business purpose, the clearest next step is to reapply after you have built up a stronger balance in your account and can demonstrate a more stable financial picture. This would likely improve your chances substantially. (218 words)
